title: A Constrained Optimization Perspective of Unrolled Transformers
claim: Enforcing layerwise descent yields monotonic loss decrease across depth and more graceful degradation under distribution shift than unconstrained training.
layout: 2 line plots side by side, shared legend in right panel
description: Two side-by-side line plots comparing a constrained model (solid blue line, circle markers) with an unconstrained baseline (dashed orange line, circle markers). Left panel: test loss, y-axis from about 0 to 0.5, against layer index, x-axis 0 to 23. The blue curve falls smoothly from about 0.4 to near 0.05. The orange curve sits flat near 0.5 until layer 14. It then drops, spikes back up around layer 18, and falls to near zero by layer 19. Right panel: test accuracy against perturbation level γ from 0 to 2.1. Both curves start near 0.96. The blue curve stays higher once γ passes about 1.2, ending near 0.56, while the orange curve falls faster, ending near 0.52. A legend sits in the lower left of the right panel. The eye goes first to the contrast between blue and orange.
caption: Layerwise descent improves OOD robustness. Left: Test loss at each layer ($\downarrow$ lower is better). Constrained RoBERTa exhibits monotonic descent, unlike the unconstrained baseline. Right: Out-of-distribution accuracy under increasing embedding perturbation levels $\gamma$ ($\uparrow$ higher is better). As $\gamma$ grows, the constrained model degrades more gracefully and retains higher accuracy. Setting: RoBERTa ($L=24$) trained on IMDb, training $\gamma=0.2$.
abstract: We introduce a constrained optimization framework for training transformers that behave like optimization descent algorithms. Specifically, we enforce layerwise descent constraints on the objective function and replace standard empirical risk minimization (ERM) with a primal-dual training scheme. This approach yields models whose intermediate representations decrease the loss monotonically in expectation across layers. We apply our method to both unrolled transformer architectures and conventional pretrained transformers on tasks of video denoising and text classification. Across these settings, we observe constrained transformers achieve stronger robustness to perturbations and maintain higher out-of-distribution generalization, while preserving in-distribution performance.
